transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Anya Reddy (Redwood CSM); Sarah Kim (Voltix Head of ML), Raj Patel (CTO), Priya Singh (Platform Eng), Tommy Lee (Data Scientist)

Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
Voltix is evaluating migration from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated / private options to reduce cost and get deterministic latency. Primary drivers: data residency, auditability, and lower per-token cost at scale. They run mix of chat + chain-of-thought generation for clinical summarization and custom fine-tuned models via vLLM/TGI. Concerned about eval parity, tokenization differences, and KMS integration.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you all taking the time. Quick roll call — I have Marco from SE, Anya from CS. Voltix folks?
[00:05] Sarah (Voltix): Sarah here. Hi.
[00:07] Raj (Voltix): Raj here. Sorry running a little late.
[00:09] Priya (Voltix): Priya on my end.
[00:11] Lena: Great. We're here to understand your migration goals from OpenAI and how Redwood Dedicated or Private could fit. Quick agenda: requirements, current stack, perf + cost targets, security/compliance, and next steps. Sound good?
[00:20] Raj: Yep. High level — we have clinical summarization pipelines and a patient Q&A bot. We've been using OpenAI for two years. Cost is becoming a big line item and we need more control over PII, plus SOC2 and audit logs for compliance.
[00:33] Marco (SE): Thanks, Raj. Can you walk us through current architecture? Where are the models hosted and what's your inference stack look like?
[00:38] Raj: Sure — front end calls our API, it proxies to a service that hits OpenAI chat completions. We do prompt chaining, we also run some on-prem inference using vLLM for a few internal models. Most heavy lifting is OpenAI. Throughput is bursty — 200 to 2,000 reqs/min, average sequence length ~800 tokens for summaries.
[00:55] Tommy (Voltix): Also we run TGI for a few experiments, especially when we need custom kernels, but it's not productionized.
[01:02] Marco: Got it. On the eval side, how do you measure parity? Do you have a set of prompts and acceptance criteria?
[01:09] Sarah: Yes. We have a holdout prompt set of ~5k clinical cases, and we score by ROUGE and human raters on hallucination and safety. Acceptance is within 5% of baseline in automated metrics and no increased hallucination.
[01:22] Marco: That's helpful. For tokenization — do you send raw clinical notes or preprocessed tokens?
[01:27] Priya: We send raw notes. We did notice some tokenization differences when we tested vLLM locally — slightly different counts vs OpenAI which affects cost and truncation behavior.
[01:36] Marco: Yeah tokenization can be tricksy. Redwood can reproduce OpenAI-compatible tokenization for many models; we also have a tokenization mapping doc we'll share. But we'll need your sample prompts and a few representative documents to run parity.
[01:49] Raj: One of our big asks is KMS/HSM integration — keys never leave our cloud. Also VPC peering.
[01:55] Lena: Understood. Redwood Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations, plus VPC peering / PrivateLink style networking. We'll include the network diagram in the pack.
[02:04] Sarah: And audit logs — we need per-request logs for two years and RBAC.
[02:08] Anya (CSM): We can talk retention tiers — we have long-term logging add-on for enterprise and RBAC modeled via SSO + SCIM.
[02:16] Priya: From a runtime view, latency matters. We need p99 < 600ms for short queries (under 200 tokens), and for the long summaries p95 < 2.2s is acceptable. Cost per token target is about 30% lower than our current OpenAI spend.
[02:31] Marco: Good to know. Quick question — are you using any streaming / function-calling features from OpenAI?
[02:36] Tommy: Yes we use streaming for the chat product, and function calling for structured extraction, it's important we keep those semantics in migration.
[02:43] Marco: Redwood supports streaming and function calling semantics; the API is intentionally similar though there are some naming differences in the SDK. We'll map those in a migration guide.
[02:51] Raj: For on-prem constraints, sometimes we run vLLM locally for ultra-sensitive cases. Is Redwood Private an option for air-gapped environments?
[02:59] Lena: Yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem deployments and an air-gapped package. There is more ops work on your side but it's supported. For Dedicated, we provide isolated GPU pools with dedicated capacity and guaranteed throughput.
[03:12] Raj: How do you handle model compatibility? Our stack uses some fine-tuned checkpoints and we also tried TGI for quantization. We care about eval parity when switching execution engines.
[03:22] Marco: We do a couple of things — first, we onboard the exact model weights where licensing allows, else we use a verified equivalent; second, we run eval parity tests with your prompt sets and report delta. Our runtime supports the common attention optimizations and quantization profiles (int8, int4) but quantization may change outputs; we surface quality-vs-cost tradeoffs.
[03:41] Sarah: Can you run vLLM-style microbenchmarks? Our engineers are concerned about KV cache management and memory behaviour under long context.
[03:49] Marco: Absolutely. Our benchmark harness can reproduce KV cache loads, long context, and the burst patterns you described. We'll share configs. One caveat — some micro-ops differ across runtimes so tiny output diffs are expected; we'll measure at metric-level not byte-for-byte.
[04:05] Priya: What about tokenizer oddities — when we switched from OpenAI to an open model locally we saw tokenization shift that made prompts exceed length limits unexpectedly.
[04:13] Marco: We'll include tokenization parity tests in the runbook. We can also provide a tokenization shim for your preprocessor if needed.
[04:20] Sarah: Security — we need SOC2 and ISO attestation, encryption in transit and at rest, and key separation for logs. Also, do you provide audit logs per token or per request?
[04:30] Anya: Audit logs are per request with metadata; we can include request/response hashes and we also support pushing logs into your SIEM via syslog or S3 export. Retention add-ons available.
[04:40] Raj: Latency vs cost — in our analysis, OpenAI gives good latency but cost is variable. How does Dedicated trade off?
[04:47] Marco: Dedicated is about predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale; you can pin capacity, and we provide autoscale/burst options. For latency, we can reserve capacity in-region and tune batching parameters to hit your p99 SLOs. We also provide smart routing to fallback to hosted for bursts if you want hybrid.
[05:04] Priya: Do you support multiple model variants to fall back when quantized models degrade?
[05:08] Marco: Yes — routing/fallback policies let you set primary/secondary model variants by latency/cost tier. Also can do canary rollouts.
[05:15] Tommy: About streaming — we saw some choppy tokens when we tried other runtimes. Is streaming stable?
[05:20] Marco: We've invested in streaming stability; we support chunked token streaming and token-level cost accounting. We'll include a sample streaming client and an SDK patch.
[05:29] Sarah: What about compliance with data residency? We need EU-only processing for some datasets.
[05:34] Lena: We have regions and can provision Dedicated capacity in EU regions, and Private deployments for fully on-prem. We'll also show the data flow and where logs live.
[05:42] Raj: Timeline — if we decide to move, how long to onboard? We have a Q1 2026 target to reduce OpenAI spend by 30%.
[05:49] Marco: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 6-8 weeks for an initial capacity and parity checks, but depends on the complexity of your fine-tunes and the VPC setup.
[05:58] Priya: Pricing — can you give an order-of-magnitude? We need to take to procurement.
[06:03] Lena: We'll follow up with a detailed pricing sheet showing reserved capacity tiers, burst pricing, and add-ons like long-term logging and private deployment fees. Expect ranges; we'll include a sample commitment that meets your 30% target.
[06:14] Raj: One more technical: how do you ensure model fingerprinting and immutability for audits? We need to show exact model versions used for a given date.
[06:23] Marco: We version artifacts, store checksums for models, and include model provenance in the audit logs. We'll provide a sample evidence bundle.
[06:32] Tommy: Any known incompatibilities with TGI or vLLM? We had to patch some kernels for certain layers earlier.
[06:38] Marco: Generally compatibility is good for most transformer-based checkpoints. Some very-custom kernels or plugin ops may need adaptors. If you share the exact checkpoint we can test and call out any code changes.
[06:50] Sarah: Risks — what are the top migration risks you see?
[06:53] Marco: I'd call out three: 1) tokenization differences causing cost or truncation changes; 2) quantization-induced quality regressions if not validated; 3) networking/security setup delays for VPC/HSM. We mitigate these with parity runs, canary policies, and a joint runbook.
[07:11] Raj: That sounds reasonable. Next steps then?
[07:14] Lena: We'll send the SOC2 + security pack, pricing, and Marco will schedule the parity deep dive. We will also ask you to share sample prompts and tokenization notes.
[07:22] Priya: We'll assemble the prompts and share by Friday.
[07:24] Raj: I'll get procurement contacts looped in.
[07:26] Anya: I'll include the onboarding checklist and contact info for ops.
[07:30] Lena: Great — thanks everyone. Quick recap in chat and we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[07:33] Sarah: Thanks all.
[07:35] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: several product names transcribed inconsistently (e.g., vLLM as v-L-L-M, TGI as T-G-I), some punctuation and speaker overlaps; overall medium quality.
